transcript: I had beef with the immersive Sweeney Todd revival from 2017 but I didn't have TikTok back then so I'm complaining about it now welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history so this famous revival of Sweeney Todd was performed at the Barrow Street Theatre now called the Greenwich House Theatre but they built up the whole space to look like a pie shop but not just any pie shop this production, which was created by Tooting Arts Club and directed by Bill Buckhurst had its origins in 2014 in London where it was performed in the real life Harrington's Pie and Mash the site-specific concept caught on so they decided to bring it to New York essentially replicating the immersive concept but now on a set the audience would sit at these long tables and for an additional price you could have a meat pie dinner before the show the New York production featured several casts with exciting Broadway talent but I got to see it with Carolee Carmello and Norm Lewis as replacements which was fantastic the production was overall very popular it ran for a year and a half but I was the one annoying naysayer here's my problem okay with any site specific theatre there comes limitations in the staging because you're working with a pre-existing space that was built for a totally different purpose and when it's actually site specific you can forgive those limitations because it's just part of the fun it comes with the territory but when you recreate that staging on a fabricated set it feels a lot less forgivable and in this case I found the staging actually extremely awkward, overly cramped it felt like they had willingly created a problem for themselves and then didn't solve it the big moment that was so egregious to me was “god that's good” which if you don't know Sweeney Todd that's the Pie Shop song the song where the pie shop is full of people and Mrs Lovett is bopping around having bits of conversations with all the different customers it's the one scene in the show that was *begging* to be done in this specific immersive configuration and they had Mrs. Lovett sing the entire song up on the staircase, away from the audience standing still like you had one job! I don't really blame the director because I think it's probably the assignment the producers gave him to recreate exactly what he had already done in the pie shop I just think on a fundamental level it didn't lend itself well to recreation and you might think it's crazy for me to look at this production of Sweeney Todd a masterwork of musical theatre performed by some of Broadway's most exciting talent and get hung up on something like the blocking but I don't think it's crazy at all because the use of physical space is what they were selling here that was the gimmick of the production I should also mention I generally don't think Sweeney Todd works as well on the small scale I'm aware that there have been many small scale productions especially following John Doyle's very influential revival but I just don't like it as much so this was already an approach to Sweeney Todd that I don't prefer and that was exponentially aggravated by everything else I just said lastly I wanna take a moment to recognize that Harrington's Pie and mash sadly closed its doors permanently only five months ago after being in operation since 1908 sad to see this beloved establishment go sad I never got to try it and sad that I didn't get to see Sweeney Todd in this space because I think I would have enjoyed it a lot more
classificationReason: Retrospective review of 2017 immersive Sweeney Todd revival, but this specific production is not on the provided list
